record.original_question: For the three-dimensional Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega, possibly convex or even strictly star-shaped, does there exist a least-energy sign-changing solution for every lambda > 0?

evidence.quote: Since it has been pointed out in [5] that the existence of least-energy sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) for N = 3 is still unknown, we also want to ask

Open question 12: In a general bounded domain Omega, if necessary, it could be convex or even strictly star-sharped, does there exist least-energy sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) for N = 3 and lambda > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain (which may, if needed, be assumed convex or even strictly star-shaped with respect to some point), and let $2^* = 6$ denote the critical Sobolev exponent in dimension three. Consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u = \lambda u + |u|^{2^*-2} u & \text{in } \Omega, \\
u = 0 & \text{on } \partial \Omega,
\end{cases}
$$
where $\lambda > 0$. A weak solution $u \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ is called sign-changing (nodal) if both $u^+ = \max(u,0)$ and $u^- = \max(-u,0)$ are nontrivial. Define the energy functional
$$
I_\lambda(u) = \tfrac{1}{2} \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx - \tfrac{\lambda}{2} \int_\Omega u^2\,dx - \tfrac{1}{2^*} \int_\Omega |u|^{2^*}\,dx,
$$
and let $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ denote the set of sign-changing weak solutions. A least-energy sign-changing solution is an element $u \in \mathcal{M}_\lambda$ minimizing $I_\lambda$ over $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$.

Question: For every $\lambda > 0$, does there exist a least-energy sign-changing solution of the above problem on every such bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of least-energy sign-changing solutions to the Brezis–Nirenberg problem in dimension $N=3$ on general bounded domains is widely acknowledged as an open problem. Partial results are known: existence has been established for specific situations such as $\lambda$ in left-neighborhoods of eigenvalues (non-coercive case) and in the three-dimensional ball (where infinitely many sign-changing nonradial solutions have recently been constructed, resolving Brezis's listed open problem on the ball). However, the general-domain case for all $\lambda>0$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Least-energy solutions for the Brézis-Nirenberg problem in dimension 3 in the non-coercive case
status_evidence.snippet: existence of least-energy sign-changing solutions of very small energy when λ belongs to a left-neighbourhood of any eigenvalue ... first general existence result for the Brézis-Nirenberg problem in dimension 3 in the non-coercive case
status_evidence.claim: Only partial existence results are known for the 3D Brezis–Nirenberg least-energy sign-changing problem.

status_evidence.title: A complete scenario on nodal radial solutions to the Brezis Nirenberg problem in low dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: existence of sign-changing solutions in the three-dimensional case (N = 3) poses challenges similar to those encountered for positive solutions, while also introducing additional complexities
status_evidence.claim: The 3D sign-changing case remains particularly challenging and is not fully resolved on general domains.
